description: cabf_tls_br.rs:RsaMinKeySizeLint uses rsa_modulus_byte_len (byte-length comparison: n_bytes >= 256 = 2048 bits). A 2047-bit RSA key has a modulus with top bit clear, but due to DER sign-byte encoding the value may still decode to 256 bytes — the leading zero is present ONLY when the top bit would be set. So a 2047-bit key actually has 256 bytes of modulus magnitude (no leading zero), measuring as 2048 bits under the byte-length check. The doc comment acknowledges this: 'a 2047-bit modulus is 256 bytes with a leading zero'. But a 2047-bit key does NOT have a leading zero (it has 256 bytes with a clear top bit). Byte-length floor at 256 passes both 2048-bit and 2047-bit keys. The doc comment is self-contradictory. Whether this violates the TLS BR (which requires 2048-bit minimum) is a real question. The lint should use rsa_public_key_bits() from pkix-path which correctly calculates bit length via UintRef (stripping the sign byte) and multiplying by 8 — this also rounds up by at most 7 bits, so it has the same lenience but is less confusing. At minimum, the doc comment is wrong and misleading.
title: RsaMinKeySizeLint: 2047-bit key passes 2048-bit floor check
